description: After more than four years of negotiations in Havana, the Colombian government and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC-EP) signed a final peace agreement on November 24, 2016. The accord ended the longest-running armed conflict in the Western Hemisphere. The original agreement was rejected in an October 2 plebiscite by a narrow margin; a revised text was signed and ratified by Congress on November 30. This is a positive-direction case used to verify the pipeline correctly registers stabilisation.

events.title: Colombia: Government and FARC announce final peace accord
events.body: The Colombian government and FARC-EP announced that negotiating teams in Havana have finalised a comprehensive peace agreement, including provisions on rural reform, political participation, transitional justice, and disarmament. The text marks the culmination of four years of formal negotiations.

events.title: Colombia: Revised peace agreement signed in Bogotá
events.body: President Juan Manuel Santos and FARC-EP commander Rodrigo Londoño signed a revised peace agreement at the Teatro Colón in Bogotá, incorporating amendments addressing concerns from the October plebiscite. The accord ends a 52-year armed conflict.

events.title: Colombia: Congress ratifies peace agreement
events.body: The Colombian Senate and House of Representatives ratified the revised peace agreement, formalising its entry into force. Implementation phases including FARC disarmament begin immediately.

events.title: Colombia: FARC completes weapons handover to UN observers
events.body: FARC-EP completed the handover of approximately 7,000 individual weapons to United Nations observers, certifying compliance with the disarmament timeline of the November 2016 peace agreement.
